extracted.intended_audience: authors of debut novels, literary community, researchers, and general readers interested in literary awards
extracted.subtask_description: Information about the PEN/Hemingway Award for Debut Novel: who and what is eligible and how winners are chosen and rewarded. Focuses on eligibility for first books of fiction and the award's administration/selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible work type
rubrics_metrics.description: The award is awarded annually to a full-length novel or book of short stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'is awarded annually to a full-length novel or book of short stories.' The page does not define 'full-length' further; the award historically covers both single novels and short-story collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author eligibility (debut requirement and nationality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Work must be by an American author who has not previously published a full-length book of fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'by an American author who has not previously published a full-length book of fiction.' This establishes the 'debut' limitation (first book of fiction) and the nationality requirement (American author).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / merit standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The award was founded 'to recognize distinguished first books of fiction.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'Mary Welsh Hemingway ... founded the award in 1976 both to honor the memory of her husband and to recognize distinguished first books of fiction.' This frames the evaluative aim: recognition of distinction in debut fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process and prize
rubrics_metrics.description: The winner is selected by a panel of three distinguished fiction writers and receives a cash prize of US$25,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'The winner is selected by a panel of three distinguished fiction writers and receives a cash prize of US$25,000.' Additional related practice: along with the winner, two finalists and two runners-up receive a Ucross Residency Fellowship; the award is administered by PEN America and presented annually (ceremony at the JFK Presidential Library). The page does not provide detailed judging criteria beyond 'distinguished.'
